compass.features.subtitle: Built-In Engineering
compass.features.desc: Standard browser dials just show raw orientation. Online Compass adds advanced user features to handle browser permission lockouts, screen pixel details, and dynamic sky projections.
compass.howItWorks.desc1: The browser captures orientation values from the absolute motion sensors. The compass rose rotates inversely relative to the heading angles, locking the needle to the top of the interface. Coordinates are queried locally, keeping location data fully private.
compass.howItWorks.desc2: Astronomy views integrate formulas to map altitude and azimuth dynamically, presenting sunrise, sunset, and moon phases without requiring third-party server computations.

prayerTimes.keywords: prayer times, salah times, fajr time, dhuhr time, asr time, maghrib time, isha time, islamic prayer times, namaz times
prayerTimes.heading: Prayer Times
prayerTimes.subtitle: Daily prayer times for your location. Select your calculation method for accurate Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha times.
prayerTimes.aboutMethods.desc: Prayer times vary by calculation method due to different Fajr and Isha solar depression angles. The Muslim World League (MWL) method is the most widely used internationally and is the default here. Select the method followed by your local mosque.
prayerTimes.educationalDesc: Prayer times are determined by the position of the sun in the sky. Each of the five daily prayers has a defined window based on solar measurements that have been used for over 1,400 years.
prayerTimes.fact1Body: Muslims pray five times daily at prescribed times tied to the sun's position: Fajr (dawn), Dhuhr (noon), Asr (afternoon), Maghrib (sunset), and Isha (night). The times shift daily with the seasons.
prayerTimes.fact2Body: Different calculation methods use different solar depression angles for Fajr and Isha. MWL uses 18° for Fajr and 17° for Isha. ISNA uses 15° for both. Choose the method followed in your community.
prayerTimes.fact3Body: The Asr prayer time is based on shadow length. The Shafi'i/Maliki/Hanbali school uses shadow = object height. The Hanafi school uses shadow = 2x object height, making Asr later.
prayerTimes.fact4Body: Prayer times vary by latitude, longitude, elevation, and calculation method. At extreme latitudes (above 48°), some methods use special adjustments to prevent excessively early or late timings.

faq.question1: Does Online Compass work on every device?
faq.answer1: It works best on mobile devices (smartphones/tablets) containing a magnetometer sensor. Desktop browsers do not expose compass data, so a phone or tablet is required for active readings.
faq.question2: Is this true north or magnetic north?
faq.answer2: Device orientation sensors report magnetic heading. True north requires a local declination correction. This site allows you to compare live orientation with coordinates.
faq.question3: Why does the compass ask for permission?
faq.answer3: For security and privacy, modern mobile browsers (especially Safari on iOS) require an explicit user gesture (a button tap) before activating device motion sensors.
faq.question4: How do I improve compass accuracy?
faq.answer4: Hold the device flat in your hand, stand away from metal structures, speakers, or magnetic fields, and move your device slowly in a figure-eight motion to calibrate.
